title: How Much Does Loopio Cost in 2026? Pricing, Features and Reviews
summary: Loopio doesn't publish prices. See 2026 plan ranges, cost per user, add-on fees, AI features, and what G2 reviewers say about it.
body_markdown:
*This guide is published by*[Inventive AI](https://www.inventive.ai/) *, an AI-native RFP response platform and Loopio alternative. Pricing data comes from third-party procurement data and verified reviews, so you can make your own call.*


Loopio doesn't publish its prices. To get a number, you book a call, sit through a demo, and wait for a custom quote, which is why Loopio pricing is one of the most searched questions in the[RFP software](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/best-rfp-software) category.


**The short answer:** Loopio's entry plan typically costs $10,000 to $20,000 a year, and the median contract is about $24,200, according to[Vendr's procurement data](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/loopio) . Contracts range from about $11,800 to $59,300 a year, and enterprise deals run $75,000 to $200,000+.


## **Key takeaways**


- **Price:** Quote-only. The entry plan runs about $10,000 to $20,000 a year, and the median contract is about $24,200.
- **Pricing unit:** Seats drive the bill, so every SME you add as a full user raises the cost. Projects are unlimited.
- **Add-ons:** Integrations, onboarding, premium support, and renewal uplifts can raise total spend 15% to 40%.
- **AI:** Loopio's AI (Response Intelligence) drafts from its content library, so answer quality depends on how well that library is maintained.
- **Reviews:** 4.6/5 on G2 across 813 reviews, with ease of use the most-praised area and AI accuracy on complex questions a common complaint.


## **What is Loopio?**


Loopio is RFP response software that helps proposal, sales, and security teams answer RFPs, RFIs, DDQs, and security questionnaires from a central library of approved content. It was founded in Toronto in 2014 by Zak Hemraj, Matt York, and Jafar Owainati, and serves more than 1,700 companies, by its own count.


Loopio isn't AI-native. It was built as a library-first platform, and its AI was added on top later. Teams store approved answers, its AI, branded Response Intelligence, suggests and drafts answers for incoming questions, and SMEs write and review anything new, which is why Loopio's strengths and hidden costs both trace back to the library.


Most of Loopio's G2 reviewers come from computer software (225 reviews), IT and services (110), and financial services (61), and about 70% are based in North America.


## **How does Loopio pricing work?**


Loopio uses quote-based, seat-driven annual subscriptions. Every purchase runs through a sales-led quote, and contracts are annual or multi-year. Four factors set what you pay:


1. **Plan tier:** Foundations, Enhanced, and Enterprise on[Loopio's pricing page](https://loopio.com/pricing/) . Procurement data still uses the older names Essentials, Plus, and Advanced for the same ladder.
2. **Seat count and user type:** Standard Users, Library Users, and Content Contributors are priced differently, and Standard seats cost the most.
3. **Add-ons:** Translations, integrations, premium support, and onboarding packages are priced separately.
4. **Negotiation:** Discounts of 10% to 30% off list are common for multi-year commitments.


Across 268 Loopio purchases in Vendr's data, the median annual contract is $24,209.

## **How much does each Loopio plan cost?**


Loopio's plans run from about $10,000 a year for Foundations to $200,000+ for Enterprise, with most mid-market teams on Enhanced at $25,000 to $100,000.


### **How much does Loopio Foundations cost?**


Foundations plan costs about $10,000 to $20,000 a year. It's built for smaller or sales-led teams and includes 10 seats, unlimited projects and library entries, and standard support, which works out to roughly $1,000 to $1,800 per standard user.


**Watch out:** Salesforce and HubSpot integrations and SSO are add-ons at this tier.


### **How much does Loopio Enhanced cost?**


Enhanced, Loopio's most popular tier, costs about $25,000 to $100,000 a year depending on seats. It adds a multi-language library, confidential projects, multi-step review workflows, and CRM integrations (Salesforce, HubSpot, Dynamics), at roughly $1,500 to $3,500 per standard user.


**Watch out:** Premium customer success typically adds $5,000 to $15,000 a year, and translations cost $100 to $300 per language per project.


### **How much does Loopio Enterprise cost?**


Enterprise costs about $75,000 to $200,000+ a year. It's built for global companies with multiple business units and adds a custom mix of user types, all integrations, dedicated account management, SSO and audit logging, and priority support. Per-user cost often drops to around $1,500 to $3,000 because of volume.


**Watch out:** Professional services for custom configuration can add $5,000 to $25,000.

## **What add-ons does Loopio charge extra for?**


Loopio's base subscription rarely matches the final bill. Commonly quoted add-ons include:


- **Salesforce integration and SSO (entry tier):** About $500 to $1,500 a year
- **Go/No-Go evaluation module:** $2,000 to $5,000 a year
- **Assist Package (premium onboarding):** $2,000 to $4,000 a year
- **Premium customer success:** $5,000 to $15,000 a year
- **Project translations:** $100 to $300 per language per project
- **Implementation and professional services:** $5,000 to $25,000 one-time
- **Annual renewal uplift:** 3% to 5% a year


Per Vendr, add-ons can raise total spend by 15% to 40%.


## **What hidden costs come with Loopio?**


The biggest hidden cost is the labor of keeping Loopio's content library accurate. Loopio's value is a curated Q&A database your team builds over time, and it works only while someone keeps it current. That ongoing work, the library management tax, compounds in four ways:


- **Curation headcount:** Someone has to review new answers, merge duplicates, tag entries, and archive stale content. If even part of a content manager's time costs $40,000 a year, a $24,000 license becomes a $60,000+ program.
- **Review cycles that never end:** Loopio's review cadence flags entries for periodic re-verification, which means recurring time from SMEs in security, legal, product, and finance after every release or policy change.
- **Stale-answer risk:** An outdated security answer in a DDQ creates legal exposure, and a deprecated feature quoted in an RFP sets your customer success team up to fail.
- **AI drafts from the same library:** Loopio's AI draws on the library, so when the library decays, the AI produces wrong answers faster.


**Rule of thumb:** Add 30% to 100% to the annual license quote for content operations labor. That's closer to your true total cost of ownership.

## **How can you negotiate a lower Loopio price?**


The biggest savings come from multi-year terms, capped renewal uplifts, and the right mix of user types. Vendr's deal data points to five levers:


1. **Bundle add-ons into the base contract:** Bundling typically saves $3,000 to $8,000 a year compared to buying add-ons later.
2. **Cap the uplift:** 70% to 80% of deals with an explicit cap land below 3%, and some at 0%.
3. **Right-size user types:** Moving occasional users to Library or Contributor seats cuts spend 10% to 20%.
4. **Commit multi-year and buy at quarter-end:** Two- to three-year terms unlock 15% to 30% in cumulative savings.
5. **Name the competition:** An active evaluation of alternatives adds another 5% to 15% on average.


## **What RFP response automation and content library features does Loopio offer?**


Loopio combines a structured content library, AI-assisted drafting, and collaboration workflows for proposal and sales teams, with integrations and governance on higher tiers.


- **Content library:** Approved answers organized in a three-tier structure (Stacks, Categories, Subcategories), with tagging, search, and freshness scoring to show how recently each entry was reviewed, plus duplicate detection and approval controls for library changes.
- **Response Intelligence (AI-assisted drafting):** Suggests library answers for incoming questions and generates first drafts, so teams start from reused content instead of a blank page.
- **Collaboration and review workflows:** Section assignments, comment threads, deadlines, and multi-step reviews for SMEs and approvers.
- **Review cycles:** Scheduled re-verification of library entries so content owners can catch outdated answers.
- **Browser extension for portals:** Imports questionnaires from procurement portals such as Ariba, Jaggaer, and UpGuard, so teams can answer without leaving Loopio.
- **Integrations:** Salesforce, HubSpot, Microsoft Dynamics, Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Teams, and Slack, with some connectors priced as add-ons on the entry tier.
- **Go/No-Go module:** An add-on that scores whether an opportunity is worth pursuing before the team commits time.
- **Analytics:** Content usage, project progress, and team activity reporting for proposal managers.


## **What do Loopio reviews say about its AI features?**


Reviewers like the time Loopio's AI saves on repeat questions, but the most common AI complaint is that drafts still need significant review on technical or highly customized questions.


Loopio's AI, branded Response Intelligence, matches incoming questions to stored answers and drafts from them. It's strongest when a question closely resembles something already in the library and weakest on novel, multi-part, or deal-specific questions. As library content ages, draft quality drops with it, which is why reviews keep tying AI performance to library upkeep.


- [Verified User in Financial Services](https://www.g2.com/products/loopio/reviews/loopio-review-11957602) **, Mid-Market (G2, Nov 2025):** "The AI capabilities have improved but still require significant review before responses are client-ready, especially for technical or highly customized questions. Library management continues to be a challenge because outdated and duplicate content accumulates over time, making answer selection less reliable. Search relevance could also be improved so the best responses surface more consistently." **‍**
- [Verified User in Computer Software](https://www.g2.com/products/loopio/reviews/loopio-review-11978792) **, Mid-Market (G2, September 2025):** "I find the interface challenging to navigate, and the AI-generated responses are not very helpful."


For buyers, the practical test is simple: run a recent RFP with a few questions your library has never answered and see how much the AI can draft without help.


## **What strengths are associated with Loopio?**


Reviewers credit Loopio with an approachable interface, real time savings on repetitive questions, and strong collaboration. It holds[4.6/5 on G2](https://www.g2.com/products/loopio/reviews) , and[4.2/5](https://www.gartner.com/reviews/vendor/loopio) on Gartner Peer Insights. The most-mentioned pros on G2 are ease of use (235 mentions), efficiency (146), and time saved (143).


- **Customer support and onboarding:** Reviewers consistently single out responsive support and hands-on account management.
- **Ease of adoption:** Often described as easier to pick up than legacy tools like Qvidian or RocketDocs.
- **Mature content library:** Centralized answers with tagging and search, a big step up for teams coming from spreadsheets and shared drives.
- **Enterprise workflow:** Multi-step reviews, confidential projects, separate business units, and SSO with audit logs suit large, regulated organizations.
- **Unlimited projects:** Every tier meters people rather than RFP volume.


**What a Loopio user likes:** Jack W., Bid Manager, Mid-Market (G2, Jun 2025): "Loopio is evolving to improve constantly. There are always updates to the system to further push automation and the quality of work produced from the system through the use of AI and connections to other business systems."


## **What concerns do buyers raise about Loopio?**


The most common concerns are seat-based pricing, AI accuracy on complex questions, and the ongoing work to keep the library current. On G2, the most-mentioned cons are missing features such as Word mapping and translation (48 mentions), search limitations (41), formatting issues (39), and export issues (35).


- **Seats penalize collaboration:** The more SMEs you bring in as full users, the more you pay.
- **High entry floor:** A practical minimum around $10,000 to $15,000 a year prices out most small teams.
- **AI added to a library-first platform:** Loopio wasn't built AI-native, and its AI drafts from stored content, so outdated or conflicting entries carry into drafts unless someone maintains the library.
- **Library upkeep:** Loopio has freshness scoring and duplicate detection, but reviewers say outdated and duplicate content still builds up and the duplicate-cleanup tool could be more intuitive.
- **Import and export friction:** Some reviewers report slow content imports and formatting fixes needed when exporting long projects into client documents.


**What Loopio users dislike:**

The Duplicate Entries feature could also be more intuitive, with clearer options for choosing which entry to keep. During Project uploads, document mapping could be more flexible when identifying questions, sections, and subsections. In addition, the Library Backup export to Word would be much more useful with stronger formatting and document-structure options, since the current output often requires substantial cleanup afterward."
- Megan W. **, Senior Bid Manager, Mid-Market (G2, Jun 2025):** "There are still document formats/styles that cannot easily be loaded into Loopio, i.e. complex Excel spreadsheets with multiple columns, Word documents with tables etc."
- [Riki Regina J](https://www.g2.com/products/loopio/reviews/loopio-review-11974992) **., Director of Contract Management, Enterprise (G2, Nov 2025):** "I don't like the proposal-building functionality. It could be more intuitive and have more AI functionality. Additionally, it would be nice if Loopio were a plug-in with Google Drive."


*All reviews from*[Loopio's G2 reviews page](https://www.g2.com/products/loopio/reviews) *.*


### **What implementation risks come with Loopio?**


The main risk is time to value. Reported rollouts take about 15 to 60 days, or 8 to 12 weeks for complex enterprise migrations, and the AI improves only after the library is built and tagged. Teams also need someone to keep content current after launch, or answer quality drifts within months.


## **Is Loopio worth the price?**


Loopio is worth it for mid-market and enterprise teams with high RFP volume, a five- or six-figure budget, and someone dedicated to owning the content library. Unlimited projects mean the cost per RFP falls as volume rises: at the $24,209 median, 50 RFPs a year works out to about $484 each, and 150 RFPs to about $161.


That matches who actually uses it: 690 of Loopio's 813 G2 reviews come from mid-market and enterprise teams, and only 93 from small businesses.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### How does Loopio handle RFIs, security questionnaires, and DDQs?


All of them run through the same project workflow and draw on the same content library, with answers tagged by topic so security, compliance, and product content can be reused across questionnaire types. The browser extension handles questionnaires inside procurement portals, and security answers usually need the most frequent review because certifications and policies change often.


### Can Loopio work as an AI sales agent?


Not as an autonomous agent. Sellers can search approved Loopio content through integrations like Slack, Microsoft Teams, and Salesforce, but Loopio is a response management tool, so it answers from the library when someone asks rather than acting on deal context by itself.


### Is Loopio's AI safe for governed enterprise use?


Its governance controls are strong on higher tiers: SSO, audit logging, role-based permissions, approval workflows for library updates, and scheduled review cycles. The weaker spot is answer accuracy, since the AI drafts from stored content and reviewers report that outdated entries still slip into drafts.


### Is Loopio mostly used by small businesses?


No. Of the 783 G2 reviewers who list company size, 690 are mid-market or enterprise and only 93 (about 12%) are small businesses, and the entry price of roughly $10,000 to $20,000 a year puts it above most small-business budgets.


### RocketDocs or Loopio: which is better for response management?


RocketDocs is built for financial services teams, with a private AI model and audit trails suited to DDQs and data residency requirements. Loopio is a broader cross-industry platform with a more approachable interface and stronger collaboration workflows.


### XaitPorter or Loopio: what's the difference?


XaitPorter is a co-authoring tool for long, structured bid documents that many writers edit at once. Loopio is built around a Q&A content library and question-by-question responses, so it fits teams answering high volumes of questionnaires.


### Conveyor or Loopio: which fits security reviews better?


Conveyor specializes in security questionnaires and a customer-facing Trust Center, while Loopio covers RFPs, RFIs, DDQs, and security questionnaires in one library.
